assessment.nobel_worthiness: DMFT exactly solves the lattice problem in the limit of infinite coordination and maps it onto a self-consistent quantum impurity problem. It gave the first controlled description of the Mott transition and of coexisting coherent and incoherent excitations. Combined with electronic-structure methods (DFT+DMFT) it is now the standard way to treat correlated d- and f-electron materials, so the originality and lasting impact are very high, and the concept is clear and teachable.
assessment.attribution: The decisive steps were the infinite-dimension limit (Metzner and Vollhardt) and the mapping onto an impurity model with self-consistency (Georges and Kotliar). The supplied credit of Georges, Vollhardt and Kotliar gives a workable three-person configuration, but it leaves out Metzner and other early contributors such as Muller-Hartmann, so some allocation is arguable.
assessment.maturity: More than three decades of development, with independent implementations in many groups and quantitative comparison to spectroscopy and transport in transition-metal oxides, heavy fermions and actinides. The method is mature and widely validated, although its accuracy depends on the impurity solver and on approximations in the combined DFT+DMFT scheme.
uncertainties: Whether the committee treats a theoretical method as a discovery or invention in the sense of the will.
How to split credit among the originators of the infinite-dimension limit and of the impurity mapping.
Predictive accuracy for specific real materials is mixed, because of double-counting and solver issues; I rely on my own recollection of this literature, not independent verification.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The continuum-model prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle was followed by the observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene. This opened moire quantum materials as a tunable platform for correlation physics, with a very large downstream literature. The theory and the experiment are both original, and the field is a significant part of present condensed-matter physics.
assessment.attribution: The prediction (Bistritzer and MacDonald) and the experimental discovery (Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators, including the first author Yuan Cao) are separable contributions. The supplied names support a prize split between theory and experiment. Cao, a student, is not credited, and other groups reproduced and extended the effect.
assessment.maturity: The experimental effects were reproduced by several groups within a few years. The mechanism of the superconductivity and the nature of the correlated states are still debated, so the interpretation is not yet stable, although the discovery of the phenomena is not in doubt. Timing is reasonable but a shade early.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism and the origin of the correlated states are unresolved.
Sample-dependent reproducibility and twist-angle disorder complicate the picture.
Whether the credited trio is the fairest allocation, since several theorists contributed to flat-band ideas around the same time.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions showed that spin-dependent tunnelling gives a large, usable resistance change. The later coherent-tunnelling MgO junctions raised the effect enormously and led to magnetic read heads and MRAM. It is a clear case of fundamental spin-polarised transport physics turned into widely used technology, and it follows naturally on the 2007 giant magnetoresistance prize.
assessment.attribution: The 1995 room-temperature results are credited to Moodera and Miyazaki, who published independently within months of each other. Parkin and the Yuasa/Djayaprawira groups made the MgO breakthrough that gave the large effect in practice. The supplied names do not include the MgO theory contributors (Butler, Mathon), so the configuration is imperfect and tied to which step one chooses to honour.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of confirmation, with commercial devices in daily use. Highly mature and not at risk of reinterpretation.
uncertainties: Whether the 1995 discovery or the later MgO-based enhancement is the decisive step.
Omission of the early Julliere result and of the MgO band-structure theorists.
The committee may view this as too close to the 2007 prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Kane-Mele proposal of a time-reversal-invariant topological insulator and the quantum spin Hall effect, followed by the HgTe/CdTe observation of edge transport, founded a large field of topological band theory. It is conceptually clean, built on symmetry and band structure, and led to the identification of many real materials through first-principles calculations. Its originality and lasting impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: The theory is clearly Kane and Mele; the experimental discovery of the quantum spin Hall state is Molenkamp's group, which confirmed the prediction by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang for HgTe. Zhang, who was key to the HgTe proposal, is deceased and so cannot be recognised, and Bernevig and Hughes are not in the supplied credit. The three-name configuration is workable but an incomplete account of the history.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed by independent experiments, including ARPES on Bi-based three-dimensional topological insulators. The concept is stable and has produced widely used material classifications. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Credit for the HgTe prediction, shared with Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, who are outside the supplied names.
Overlap with the neighbouring quantum anomalous Hall candidates, which concern a separate experimental achievement.
Practical applications are still limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of a skyrmion lattice in chiral magnets, first by neutron scattering in MnSi and then by real-space imaging, together with the theory of emergent electrodynamics and the spin-transfer-torque-driven motion, established topological magnetic textures as a new state of matter. It is directly in my area. The physics is conceptually original and links to spintronic concepts such as low-current-density manipulation.
assessment.attribution: The lead experimental discovery in MnSi came from the Pfleiderer group (with Muhlbauer as first author), with theory by Rosch and collaborators, and Tokura's group provided real-space imaging and room-temperature-relevant materials. Bogdanov's early theory of chiral skyrmions is not in the supplied names. Credit is shared and fairly contested, which weakens a clean configuration.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced in many materials, but application to devices is still unproven and the strongest claims for technology are not yet realised. Recognition is plausible but somewhat early.
uncertainties: Bogdanov's precedent and the role of the first-author experimental team.
Whether the technological promise will materialise.
Relation to other topological-magnetism work, with overlapping credit across groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of superconductivity in LaFeAsO(F) and the quick raising of Tc above 50 K in related iron pnictides created the second family of high-Tc superconductors. It showed that high-temperature superconductivity is not limited to copper oxides and spurred a major effort in correlated multi-orbital and magnetic-fluctuation physics. The discovery is clear and important, though the physics is less transformative than the cuprate discovery.
assessment.attribution: Hosono's group made the original discovery in 2008. The rapid rise to 43-55 K through rare-earth substitution is credited to Chen and Zhao and their colleagues, and several groups contributed within weeks. A two-person configuration of Hosono and Zhao is defensible, but there is a case for Chen as well.
assessment.maturity: Many independent confirmations and a very large literature. The pairing mechanism remains unsettled, and no application has displaced existing materials. Timely as a discovery recognition.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity is still debated and the Nobel record favours resolved physics.
Allocation among the groups that rapidly raised Tc.
Limited technological impact so far.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, proposed by Katori using the magic wavelength, combines trapped neutral atoms with an optical transition to reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18. It pushes precision measurement, with uses in relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and a likely redefinition of the second. The idea is original and the achievement has had lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori made the key proposal and first demonstrations; Ye's group demonstrated the best systematic control and pushed the performance record. The two-name list is natural, although the earlier ion-clock work and the contributions of other groups (e.g. Ludlow, Hinkley and others) are part of the story.
assessment.maturity: Independently realised by several national laboratories and compared across continents. Highly mature, with redefinition of the second under discussion. Timeliness is good, although the 2005 prize touched frequency combs, which may be seen as adjacent.
uncertainties: How the committee weighs the adjacency to the frequency-comb and ion-clock prizes.
Allocation relative to the ion-clock community.
This lies outside my own research area, so my judgement rests on general knowledge.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Current-induced spin-transfer torque allows magnetisation to be switched or driven without a magnetic field, and underlies spin-torque MRAM and spin-torque oscillators. The concept is original and important for both the fundamental dynamics of magnets (including the atomistic and micromagnetic modelling I work with) and for devices. It is a strong magnetism and spintronics candidate.
assessment.attribution: The theoretical prediction came independently from Berger and Slonczewski in 1996. The supplied names include Berger but not Slonczewski, and, as far as I recall, Berger has died, which would complicate an eligible and fair configuration. Experimental demonstration is credited to Buhrman and Ralph and their groups, along with Tsoi and others, so credit is unresolved and difficult.
assessment.maturity: Many independent confirmations and a commercial product line. The physics is well understood, although the leading theorists may not be eligible, which affects whether a fair prize is possible.
uncertainties: Eligibility and attribution problems if Berger (and possibly Slonczewski) are deceased, which I recall but have not verified.
Credit for the first experimental observations, such as Tsoi and colleagues, versus Ralph and Buhrman.
Overlap with spin-orbit-torque developments which are not covered by this candidate.
